meta_description:
171 likes, 7 comments - gizmodo on October 29, 2026: "According to a report from the Religion News Service, a research administrator at the University of Kentucky successfully received a religious exemption from his employer, excusing him from any expectations to use AI for his work. The man, 45-year-old David Durman, identifies as a humanist and told Religion News Service that he felt being asked to use AI tools like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, as the University of Kentucky reportedly encouraged its employees to utilize, undermined his belief in the importance of the human parts of life and ran counter to his desire to see human flourishing.

In the letter he submitted to the University of Kentucky’s Office of Equal Opportunity as part of the accommodation request, Durman stated, “Substituting automated machine processing for human presence, authentic listening, and personal responsibility in my work directly conflicts with my obligation to uphold human dignity and flourishing as primary.”

Read more at the link in our bio 📲

Story: AJ Dellinger".
